bullets.title: META Muse drives record monthly gain; Goldman desk piles into Agentic AI theme
bullets.body: META gained ~32.7% this month—its strongest performance since 2013—on the back of the new Muse AI app launch. Goldman's desk flagged Agentic AI as the most-talked-about theme, with the Consumer Inertia short basket (GSXUSWCH) down 2.58% and active trading in recent sessions. Meta is also building the 5GW 'Hyperion' (Project Beignet) data center, targeting the world's largest facility by the 2030s.

bullets.title: META Muse adds PayPal and Expedia integrations; Zuckerberg attends Xi state dinner
bullets.body: Meta announced partnerships with PayPal and Expedia granting Muse AI agent access to travel and payments. Zuckerberg is also set to attend the White House state dinner for China's President Xi, signaling continued Big Tech engagement with US-China diplomacy. Meta also removed 3.7M accounts in coordination with Singapore Police.

bullets.title: NVDA forward P/E at decade-low 15.75x; insider sells $300M; bullish options flow
bullets.body: NVDA's forward P/E is now 15.75, the lowest in over a decade, even as MU and NVDA showed the strongest bullish options flow of the session. Offsetting the valuation narrative, board member Mark Stevens—a long-standing director and one of the largest shareholders—dumped $300M in shares. Separately, AVGO expects 100% supply-constrained YoY growth for the next two years while NVDA guides to 70% supply-constrained growth next year.

bullets.title: Michael Burry increases shorts on MU, NBIS, and PLTR
bullets.body: Burry disclosed added short positions in Micron (MU), Nebius (NBIS), and Palantir (PLTR), and is reportedly bearish on the broader semiconductor ETF (SOXX). This comes even as MU rallied for a sixth consecutive session alongside NVDA in driving the Nasdaq 100 to its first record close since June.

bullets.title: MSFT upgraded to Buy at Stifel, PT $575; launches AI 'super app' with boosted Copilot discounts
bullets.body: Stifel upgraded Microsoft to Buy and raised its price target to $575, citing sustainable mid-to-upper-teens revenue growth driven by LLM advancement and Azure's positioning as LLM-agnostic. Separately, The Information reports Microsoft is launching an AI 'super app' and boosting Copilot discounts to drive adoption.

bullets.title: AAPL iPhone 18 Pro sees 60-70% YoY sales surge in Taiwan; TSMC 2nm in production
bullets.body: Taiwan Mobile and Far Eastone reported 70% YoY increases in iPhone 18 Pro first-three-day sales, with Chunghwa Telecom up 60%, per media reports. TSMC's 2nm chips are confirmed shipping in iPhone 18 Pro as well as Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 devices. AAPL also hit a new all-time high with market cap above $5T.

bullets.title: AMD joins the $1 trillion market cap club; INTC flagged as compelling risk/reward
bullets.body: AMD's market cap crossed $1 trillion, hitting a 52-week high. One analyst argued INTC remains among the best risk/reward setups since the AI moment began, drawing comparisons to their AMD call at $12; Melius' Ben Reitzes published detailed INTC foundry valuation work. INTC and AMD also both hit 52-week highs today.

bullets.title: MU and SNDK prices seen above expectations in late 2026-2027; silicon wafer prices to rise 15-25%
bullets.body: Checks suggest MU and SNDK pricing in Q3/Q4 2026 could exceed expectations and continue rising into Q1 2027. Separately, 12-inch epitaxial wafer prices are forecast to rise 15-25% in 2027 as memory and logic chip capacity expansions drive demand. JPMorgan updated its HBM model, now expecting 16Hi HBM adoption no sooner than 2029.

bullets.title: NBIS hiking GPU pricing up to 20%; B300 on-demand rates at highest seen
bullets.body: NBIS is implementing up to 20% price increases on H200 and H100 on-demand rates (H200 +19.1%, H100 +16.5%), with B300 pricing at all-time highs versus peers. Prior price hike announcements drove the stock up $20+. H100 is characterized as obsolete against new Rubin clusters.

bullets.title: Taiwan August export orders surge 71.4% YoY to record $103B on AI chip demand
bullets.body: Taiwan's August export orders hit $102.96B, up 71.4% YoY and well above the 63% consensus estimate, with custom ASIC chip design orders driving the upside surprise. The data reinforces the demand narrative for TSM and NVDA supply chain names.

bullets.title: AMZN: market pricing only AWS + Anthropic value, zero for other assets; AWS set for VM pricing leverage
bullets.body: One analyst argues AMZN is effectively trading at AWS + Anthropic stake value with zero assigned to its other business lines. AWS—with the largest fleet capacity—is positioned to gain meaningful pricing leverage from VM infrastructure demand as agentic AI scales.

bullets.title: GEV accelerates $200B backlog target to early 2027; contracted gas turbines guidance seen conservative
bullets.body: GEV now expects to reach $200B of backlog by early 2027, pulling forward from the previous 2027 target. Gross new contract additions guidance of 20 GW appears conservative; GEV is likely to exit the year above 125 GW in contracted gas turbines.

bullets.title: QCOM partners with Mastercard on agentic payments; CEO touts 1M token/day device compute
bullets.body: QCOM is teaming with MA to build agentic payments infrastructure across Snapdragon phones, PCs, glasses, and cars, with MA providing the trusted payment layer. QCOM CEO Cristiano Amon emphasized that agentic AI devices may process up to 1M tokens per day, requiring new High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) chip architecture.

bullets.title: CART (Instacart) flagged as most vulnerable internet name on EBITDA margin risk
bullets.body: One analyst argues Instacart has the highest EBITDA downside risk in internet, given ad revenue's disproportionately large share of both GTV and EBITDA. Ad-revenue concentration means any slowdown compounds quickly versus peers, making it the 'longest to fall' in a sector the analyst views as a shorting opportunity.

bullets.title: Fed unexpectedly hiked last week; markets now price additional hike by year-end
bullets.body: Markets started 2026 pricing two Fed rate cuts but the Fed delivered a 25 bps hike last week, with markets now pricing at least one more hike before year-end. The author notes Trump had favored dovish Fed leadership, but new leadership appears hawkish—a reversal of early-2026 rate-cut expectations.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz near-shutdown: only 2-3 vessels vs. 125 daily pre-conflict average
bullets.body: Only 2-3 commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, compared to a pre-conflict average of ~125 large commercial ships per day—a ~98% collapse in traffic. Iran set conditions for reopening including lifting the US naval blockade, releasing frozen assets, and ending all regional conflicts. Diplomatic talks are ongoing through mediators at the UN General Assembly.

bullets.title: Crude oil 7-day losing streak (longest since Aug 2021); diesel at all-time high $6.53/gallon
bullets.body: Crude is on pace for its 7th consecutive red session—the longest losing streak since August 2021—with WTI near $94.59/bbl and Brent settling around $99.25. Diesel hit a new all-time high of $6.53/gallon, up 76% YoY, with Goldman warning a refining capacity crisis could prolong elevated fuel prices through 2027. The Trump administration is also examining a diesel export ban.

bullets.title: Institutional equity allocation at 57.4%—highest since dot-com bubble; market breadth deteriorating
bullets.body: Institutional investors now hold a 57.4% equity allocation, the highest level since the dot-com era, a potential overallocation risk signal. Market breadth is simultaneously deteriorating with six consecutive days of more 52-week lows than highs, even as the Nasdaq 100 hit its first record close since June. BTIG warns of dynamics 'last seen in January 2000.'

bullets.title: AI frontier model pricing collapses: GPT-6 Sol/Luna cut 50%; Opus 5.5 released at 40% lower cost
bullets.body: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol and Luna with token prices cut 50% versus the 5.6 family, while Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22, matching Fable 5.1 performance at 40% lower cost than Opus 5, with the strongest alignment scores in behavioral audits. One observer called it an 'insane day in AI' as per-task costs dropped rapidly across the frontier.

bullets.title: AWS becomes first cloud provider approved for NATO RESTRICTED workloads across all 32 members
bullets.body: Amazon Web Services has been approved for NATO RESTRICTED workloads across all 32 NATO member nations, a significant enterprise/government cloud milestone that could support AWS's defense and sovereign cloud revenue pipeline.
